jobs.prompt: A full-bleed illustration that fills the entire frame edge to edge, with no border, no margin and no paper edge. An oil painting made in the old masters' way for a book plate: a warm raw-umber toned ground and a brown monochrome underpainting, with bold dark brush-ink contours on the figures and the main shapes. The shadows are thin, flat, transparent glazes of umber and dark blue with the warm ground glowing through; only the lit parts are painted with opaque, thicker paint. Large calm simple shapes, broad unbroken shadow masses, very little detail, deep chiaroscuro, realistic proportions, grim and serious. Night, two thousand years ago. From the near rim of a great raw cut dug into a hillside we look down across it. At the left, close to us, two ancient soldiers stand on our rim with their backs to us, dark shapes in rust-red wool cloaks and dull bronze helmets with crests and cheek guards; one holds a small torch low in front of him. Across the cut, a long column of tiny figures carrying torches winds down the far wall in an S-shaped path to the bottom of the picture; the torches are the brightest things in the picture. The far wall is a few big flat planes of dark rock. Above it the dark hillside rises to a crest under a strip of night sky. Torch smoke drifts. The orange torchlight is the only strong color; everything else is night.

Large calm simple shapes, broad unbroken shadow masses, very little detail, deep chiaroscuro, realistic proportions, grim and serious. Dusk, a deep blue sky over a thin dull rose band above the far hills. A small camp beside a rutted dirt track: a campfire burning high, a bedroll with its blanket folded on top, a pack. A lone traveler sits on a log by the fire with their back to us, the whole body wrapped from the hood to the ground in one plain dark wool hooded cloak, a simple cone shape, the head bowed over a folded letter held to the firelight; a small flask hangs on a cord from one wrist. Far up the track, the warm lamps of a waystation, one lamp higher than the rest. Low through the bare trees on the right, by the water, three small points of cold blue light. The fire's orange is the warm color; the rest is blue dusk.

Large calm simple shapes, broad unbroken shadow masses, very little detail, deep chiaroscuro, realistic proportions, grim and serious. Night, hard frost on a field beside a pale road, small ember-gold glints scattered in the frozen soil. A dead villager stands upright, slack, arms hanging, head tilted, in a torn linen shirt; his gray face is blank, the mouth hanging open and the empty eye sockets glowing with soft golden light from inside, his skin lit from within like paper over a lamp. To the right an old watchman with a gray beard, in a slate blue-gray hooded cloak over a plain wool tunic, a matte round wooden shield with a dull iron boss on his arm, leans in with his weight forward and both hands on a plain dark spear whose head is buried in the dead man's chest; golden light bursts out around the shaft and pours down onto the frost as small glowing stones. A pale white plume of breath leaves the watchman's mouth. The golden light is the only strong color; the rest is cold night, frost and slate.
